Add an authenticated evidence-graph worker that turns a Gmail message into a bounded cross-surface case: preserve message/thread ID and link origins, open only same-origin authenticated links, extract selected fields with DOM/source citations, hand a normalized case to Mac diagnostics, and join returned local evidence into one immutable incident or dispute packet. It must support pause/resume, deduplication, and an explicit draft-not-submitted state rather than a generic page summary.

Add an extension-side privacy firewall that classifies DOM nodes before any browser result is posted: redact passwords, auth tokens, payment numbers, hidden inputs, and unrelated off-screen regions; return typed placeholders plus locator hashes, while allowing the owner to explicitly request a narrowly scoped reveal for one field.

Add a user-visible browser task checkpoint that snapshots the active tab set, extracted field values, scroll/step position, and pending reversible actions after every successful browser command. On Safari reconnect, offer ‘resume the browser task’ from the pendant or Mac, revalidate URL and key page anchors before continuing, and mark any changed field/page as needing re-inspection instead of blindly replaying clicks.

Make authenticated Safari extraction resilient to protected/isolated frames: when browser_read_page or snapshot receives ‘extension does not have access to this frame’, automatically retry through an extension-injected content script on the top frame, then use accessibility-tree or visible-text extraction as a fallback, returning a typed ‘partial/unavailable’ result with the frame URL instead of a generic failure.

Add a local “minimum necessary page” compiler in the Safari bridge. Before any browser_read_page/snapshot result leaves the Mac, classify DOM fields and replace password inputs, payment numbers, authentication tokens, personal identifiers, and hidden/offscreen content with typed placeholders. Permit an explicit per-request selector/region allowlist, emit a redaction manifest with tabId, URL origin, and hashes, and fail closed when a page cannot be classified rather than uploading raw HTML.

Add a Safari-extension diagnostics and recovery path for frames that reject content-script execution: on a failed browser_read_page/browser_snapshot, return the tab's frame tree and permission state, retry the top document after activating the tab, and expose an explicit Safari host-permission repair action (open the extension's Website Access settings and verify the origin). Persist the failure reason and origin in the browser inspection record so the planner can stop retrying blindly.

When Safari content scripts cannot access a private frame, add an accessibility-tree extraction fallback through the extension's native tab API, returning visible roles, labels, values, and links with tabId/URL provenance. Exclude password fields and offscreen/hidden nodes, and mark results as accessibility-derived so planners do not confuse them with DOM text.

Add a verified read-only fallback chain for Safari: when browser_snapshot/read_page returns frame-access failure, collect the tab’s accessibility tree or print/reader representation through the extension, tag the result with tabId/URL/timestamp, and return a typed blocker if all fallbacks fail. Add a self-test page and expose the extension’s host-permission/frame-access diagnosis in the receipt.

Make every browser command carry an explicit target policy and resolve it at execution time: active tab, pinned session tab, or tabId. Before dispatch, return the chosen tabId/title/URL; reject silently falling back to the default Gmail session when Safari’s active tab differs. Persist the target in the receipt and verify the result came from that same tab.

Add a read-only /browser/compare operation that accepts up to six existing session/tab IDs plus typed field intents (date, amount, status, identifier), runs extraction in parallel, normalizes locale/time zone/currency, and returns per-field values with URL, tabId, title, timestamp, and source excerpt. It must report disagreement rather than pick a winner.

Add an owner-invoked active-tab change stream: Safari emits navigation plus debounced accessibility/DOM-region diffs for the current tab for a lease of at most 15 minutes; server redacts inputs and forwards only changed headings, alerts, and selected regions to the voice pipeline. Include explicit start/stop events and a byte/token budget.

Add an offline-command quarantine and reconnect watchdog around the existing browser queue. When heartbeat expires, stop accepting new mutating commands, mark the five currently pending commands as paused (not failed), notify the relay/pendant with count and oldest age, and require a fresh session/tab fingerprint before replay. On reconnect, reconcile each command by idempotency key and discard commands whose URL/session or precondition hash changed; retain safe read-only commands for bounded replay. Add a visible drain/clear action and TTL-based expiry so stale private-page work cannot execute days later.

Add reconnect quarantine for pending browser commands: every queued command gets an expiry, session/tab fingerprint, and intended effect class; when the extension reconnects, do not replay stale or write/submit commands automatically. Move them to a reviewable queue, revalidate the tab/session fingerprint, and let the relay ask the pendant whether to discard, refresh evidence, or resume. Read-only idempotent commands may be auto-replayed only within a short TTL and unchanged session.

Add a browser-bridge liveness gate and queue reconciler: when heartbeat is absent, stop retrying commands, mark them waiting-for-device (not failed), coalesce duplicate idempotent requests, and notify the relay with the exact pending count. On reconnect, perform a read-only tab/session handshake, replay only commands whose lease and idempotency key are still valid, and expire stale commands with a pendant-readable explanation. Expose a one-click/dashboard drain or cancel operation rather than leaving seven opaque pending commands.

Add a browser-bridge readiness gate and command watchdog before enqueue: require an online poll heartbeat newer than a short TTL, an attached tab/window identity, and zero stale pending commands; otherwise do not enqueue. Give each command a deadline shorter than the 45-second transport timeout, cancel/expire it explicitly, and surface a structured blocked receipt with the exact recovery (open Safari, enable bridge, dismiss dialog, or reattach tab). Add a sweeper for orphaned pendingCommands so failed browser work cannot accumulate and later run against a different tab.

Add a fast, non-mutating browser preflight gate before any browser_* step: verify the selected session/tab's bridge heartbeat, tab identity, and command-poll age within a short deadline (for example 2 seconds), then classify it as ready, stale, offline, or blocked-dialog. Do not enqueue a 45-second navigate when the bridge is known unavailable. For public URLs only, route a clearly labeled fallback to the server browser backend; for authenticated URLs, fail immediately with a one-line owner-repair instruction and preserve the intended action without retrying. Record the preflight result in the job receipt.

Implement a reconnect quarantine for pending browser commands. When the extension heartbeat returns, stop automatic execution, inventory all queued commands with request/idempotency key, target tab/session, age, and intended mutation, compare them with relay/Mac transaction records, and mark each as duplicate, stale, safe-to-resume, or requiring fresh approval. Resume only read-only or explicitly re-approved mutations; publish a reconciliation brief and preserve a per-command audit trail.

Introduce a deny-by-default, task-scoped capability broker between faculty-judgement and the authenticated browser extension. It should compile a signed manifest (allowed origins, tab/session, read selectors, writable fields, verbs, maximum mutations, expiry, and action hash), enforce it inside browser_run_actions and the extension—not merely in prompts—and emit a proof for every allowed/denied command. Revocation must propagate through the relay and invalidate queued Mac/browser work.

Add a reconnect quarantine for queued browser commands: every command gets an enqueue timestamp, bridge-session fingerprint, and intent risk class. When the extension returns after being offline, expired or session-mismatched commands remain held; the relay produces a compact review packet showing what would have run, why it was held, and whether the page changed. Only an explicit owner approval or a newly compiled idempotent plan may release a held command. Revalidate page identity and expected preconditions immediately before replay.

Add a tab-identity quarantine before any authenticated read or mutation: require a fresh extension heartbeat whose tabId, URL, title, session binding, and content hash agree with the durable session record; on contradiction, freeze commands, mark the tab orphaned, and ask the owner to choose the authoritative tab.

Implement a local payload firewall between browser planning and execution: extract candidate form fields, classify each as required/optional and sensitivity tier, generate a canonical payload hash plus a minimized payload, and require an approval token bound to tabId, URL, DOM revision, payload hash, and expiry before irreversible submit.

Add a reconnect reconciliation gate between the existing browser command queue and result/heartbeat routes. Persist for every pending command: read-vs-mutate class, creation/expiry time, originating tab URL/title hash, session id, and an idempotency key. When heartbeat returns after offline time, automatically replay only non-sensitive idempotent reads whose tab/session fingerprint still matches; mark writes, sends, and stale commands as held with an explicit reason. Emit typed queue-state events to /pipeline/events and surface the count/reasons in dashboard and pendant status. Enqueue must never be reported as completion.

Add an uncertainty quarantine for browser commands that remain queued while the extension is offline: attach enqueue time, tab/session identity, and a precondition snapshot; on reconnect, revalidate the target tab and page before execution, expire commands whose session cannot be reattached, and surface them as 'not run' rather than replaying blindly. Keep this separate from the durable runner itself.

Add an offline-queue reconciliation layer to the existing browser command queue: when home-chrome is offline, freeze commands rather than allowing blind replay; stamp each command with enqueue age, originating session/tab identity, and destructive/reversible class; expire or require fresh owner confirmation after a configurable TTL; on reconnect emit a compact review receipt listing 9 held commands and their intended targets before any replay.

Add lease expiry and quarantine semantics to browser command polling. A claimed command gets a short lease with heartbeat; if the extension is offline or no result arrives before the lease, atomically return it to queued once, then move it to stale/needs-review after a bounded retry count. Expose command age, lease expiry, attempts, and last-seen extension time in /browser/status and /browser/poll. Never hand a command marked processing to a second consumer without an idempotency key, and never let a four-hour-old command keep appearing as live work.

Add a durable pending-command lease and reconciliation loop: every browser command gets an expiry, extension heartbeat binding, and terminal state (expired/replayed/cancelled). When the extension is offline, do not leave commands indefinitely pending; surface the count and safely expire or require explicit retry once the same session returns.

Implement an offline-command quarantine: when the browser heartbeat goes offline, stop presenting pending commands as runnable, attach an expiry and originating request/session to each queued item, and require a fresh heartbeat plus tab/session revalidation before release. Mark the existing 12 home-chrome commands as quarantined rather than silently replaying them after reconnect; provide a single 'discard stale / review individually / release safe reads' decision.

Replace the bridge's split tab reporting with one atomic TabAttestation message: read tabId/windowId, URL, title, frame origin, document readiness, and a bounded content digest in the same extension turn; attach heartbeat sequence, extension instance id, and monotonic timestamp. Reject cached session metadata when its sequence or tab identity differs, and expire attestations after 10 seconds.

Add a navigation truth guard to the Safari bridge: every open/read/click transaction records the tab's pre-state, command id, post-state URL/title, and a compact DOM/page-result hash. Mark completion as failed (not successful) when the tab remains on an error title such as “Failed to open page,” the URL did not change when navigation was requested, or the post-state heartbeat is older than the command. Return the exact failing edge and preserve the receipt for retry.

Implement an offline-bridge recovery controller around browser jobs: on transport failure, classify the failure using the Mac agent's live status (extension offline, Accessibility/Screen Recording missing, browser not running, or relay unavailable); launch/open the selected browser and bridge onboarding when safe; wait for a heartbeat lease; resume only the uncompleted checkpoint with the same request/idempotency key; and emit pendant/dashboard progress plus a final receipt. Add a hard 'completed-but-no-ack' state that never replays a submit/send step.

Add a live capability preflight and fast-fail/queue path before browser_* execution. The Mac agent already reports browser online=false with 3 pending commands, while a failed navigate currently spends ~45 seconds before returning an error. On every browser job, bind it to the heartbeat/device, check extension freshness and tab/session availability, then either execute, enqueue durably with a paused receipt, or immediately report “blocked: browser bridge offline”; when heartbeat returns, resume idempotently and attach the result to the original job. Keep local Mac actions independent so a mixed job can continue its non-browser steps.

Make browser execution offline-aware: before dispatch, consult the bridge heartbeat and return a typed unavailable state immediately when offline; move queued commands into a durable pending state with TTL and owner-visible count instead of holding an HTTP request for 45 seconds. When the extension heartbeats again, reconcile commands by idempotency key, emit progress, and expire stale reads safely. Keep mutations blocked from automatic replay and surface them as needing review.

Add reconnect fencing for the browser bridge: every heartbeat issues a device epoch and lease token; poll claims must include that epoch; commands claimed by an offline or expired extension are quarantined, never replayed automatically, and require explicit reattachment to the same session/tab before retry. Expose pending, quarantined, expired, and replayed counts in /browser/status and dashboard.

Implement a causal recovery ledger and fail-fast reconciler between the existing relay/Mac job and browser queues. On enqueue, assign one intentId and per-step idempotency key; persist edges intentId→jobId→actionId→commandId. On browser heartbeat/poll/result, reconcile each step into completed, failed-before-delivery, delivered-unknown, or completed-with-evidence. If status is offline, return immediately with a resumable checkpoint instead of waiting 45 seconds. On reconnect, replay only steps marked safe-to-retry, quarantine delivered-unknown writes, and emit a local recovery capsule through /capture containing the exact evidence and next action.

Implement a Browser Bridge circuit-breaker and reconciliation worker between the existing command queue and job receipts. On each heartbeat, classify the bridge as online, stale, or offline; assign every command a creation time, TTL, idempotency key, session/tab binding, and mutation class; persist a state machine queued→leased→acknowledged→completed/failed/quarantined. When the bridge returns, automatically retry only expired-safe read steps whose binding and request hash are unchanged, quarantine all mutating steps, and emit one compact interruption receipt listing what ran, what did not, and why. Reconcile the current seven pending commands on startup rather than replaying them blindly.

Implement a reconnect-safe browser work capsule and release protocol between the existing command queue and job receipts. At enqueue, persist a capsule per step containing request/idempotency key, session+tab affinity, read/write class, URL/title/DOM fingerprint, and a redacted evidence pointer. On browser heartbeat, require a fresh tab identity and fingerprint; automatically release only idempotent reads/navigation, mark all mutations quarantined, and emit one deduplicated pipeline event plus a pendant-sized receipt. Expired or mismatched capsules are discarded with an explicit reason instead of replayed.

Replace browserBridge's single 45-second waitForBrowserResult with a leased, event-driven job state machine. On dispatch, persist commandId/action idempotency key/session id and a short lease; emit queued/dispatched/acknowledged/completed/abandoned events; renew the lease on extension heartbeat; on reconnect reconcile command receipts before retrying. Expire commands without a live lease and mark sessions detached when lastSeenAt is older than the lease window. Expose non-blocking GET job progress and a bounded stream for the planner.

Add a bridge-health lease and dead-letter watchdog, distinct from the command queue: treat a heartbeat with tabId/windowId null, missing browserName, or an old lastSeenAt as degraded even when online=true; stop claiming queued commands, mark the existing 9 pending commands as quarantined with their request IDs, and require a fresh tab-bound heartbeat epoch before replaying only idempotent reads. Surface a single repair action in the dashboard and a concise pendant notification.

Add a privacy-aware circuit breaker and queue reconciler between the existing browser routes: before dispatch, label each step public or authenticated; when /browser/status is offline, immediately divert only public steps to /research, persist private steps with idempotency keys and a resumable cursor, stop retry storms, and publish one pendant-readable state transition. On heartbeat, reconcile pending command IDs against job receipts, expire commands whose tab/session is stale, and resume only read-only steps automatically; keep mutations paused for explicit owner review.

Add a reconnect watchdog and stale-command quarantine for the browser bridge. On every heartbeat transition offline→online, atomically inspect pending commands, expire entries past TTL, mark attempts with a stable idempotency key, replay only commands whose tab/session preconditions still match, and emit one aggregate receipt for skipped/failed items. If the extension stays offline, surface a single actionable alert rather than allowing an unbounded queue (currently 9 pending commands).

Insert a fail-closed privacy firewall between the browser bridge and every research/realtime request. Each extraction returns a redacted payload plus a signed manifest containing policy version, source tab/session, withheld categories, byte counts, and a hash of the original region map; the relay accepts the payload only when the manifest attests that raw DOM, screenshots, form values, and clipboard data were not included. Keep the original and region map on the Mac, expose a local review/rollback endpoint, and emit the manifest hash into the existing job and pipeline receipts.

Add a browser-device lease and command-reconciliation layer. Treat a heartbeat as valid only when it carries a fresh device epoch plus a real tab/window identity and capability hash; mark the current home-chrome lease stale when tabId/tabUrl/tabCount are null or the heartbeat expires. Move commands claimed by that lease into a quarantined state (never execute them on a later device by accident), then requeue them with the same idempotency key only after a new valid heartbeat. Emit one durable reconciliation record per command with claimed lease, quarantine reason, retry count, and final disposition, and expose a compact status endpoint for the pendant/Mac planner. This is the missing control plane beneath the still-unbuilt durable browser runner—not an approval gate.

Add an offline-queue circuit breaker and stale-command reconciler. When browser/status reports offline or a command exceeds its deadline, stop issuing retries, atomically mark the command blocked_on_surface with the last heartbeat and reason, and expose a single resumable queue entry. On the next heartbeat, revalidate tab/session affinity and page identity before replaying only idempotent reads; discard or require a new explicit plan for writes. Also alert the relay/pendant once, not once per retry.

Add a browser-bridge liveness watchdog and queue quarantine layer, distinct from the command protocol itself. Track each device heartbeat lease and each command claim lease; when the lease expires, atomically move processing commands to `orphaned` (not immediately runnable), stop claiming new commands while the device is offline, and mark sessions whose lastUsedAt exceeds a configurable TTL as stale. On reconnection, require a fresh heartbeat and device/session identity before offering quarantined commands; replay only idempotent commands with the original request/idempotency key, while non-idempotent commands remain held for review. Emit one durable incident/receipt linking the command, attempts, last heartbeat, and reason, and let the pendant/relay announce a compact “browser bridge offline; N queued, M held” status rather than timing out for 45 seconds.

Add an explicit browser-surface readiness and recovery state machine. When the extension heartbeat reports only its own protected extension page, classify the browser as connected-but-not-user-tab-ready; preserve the last usable tab/session, expose the reason, and let a queued job wait for a real web tab instead of attempting browser_snapshot and producing a misleading failure. On recovery, revalidate origin, tabId, and session affinity before continuing.

Add a first-class ‘owner-marked page capsule’ path separate from polling watches: the Safari extension sends only the selected tab’s title, URL, visible text regions, and a redaction manifest; the Mac stores an encrypted, expiring capsule and returns a stable citation id. Relay questions can retrieve only that capsule, not browse the account afresh.

Add a fail-fast preflight and reconciliation layer before browser actions are dispatched. The Mac bridge publishes a signed capability heartbeat (extension online, session/tab identity, queue depth, last-seen age); the relay planner converts an offline or stale heartbeat into a waiting dependency instead of sending the action. On reconnect, reconcile each queued command by requestId/idempotencyKey against browser receipts, mark completed commands, and execute only unacknowledged steps. Emit blocked/resumed/expired events to the pendant and dashboard.

Add an offline-queue reconciliation state machine to browserBridge/browserSessions: every queued command gets createdAt, TTL, originating request, tab fingerprint, and intended effect class; while the extension is offline the queue is visibly 'held' rather than silently pending. On reconnect, revalidate the tab/session fingerprint, collapse idempotent duplicates, expire stale commands with a receipt, and publish a compact reconciliation event to the relay/pendant. Do not auto-replay a command whose target tab changed or whose TTL elapsed; preserve it for explicit re-planning.

Add a synchronous browser preflight and circuit breaker in the Mac/browser bridge: before enqueueing any browser_* action, consult the latest heartbeat/status, return a typed OFFLINE result immediately when no extension has polled recently, and mark queued commands as blocked_until_online rather than letting them time out after ~45 seconds. On the next heartbeat, retry each command with its original session/request id and emit one receipt linking the preflight failure, retry, and final result. Expose a compact readiness object (extension age, pending count, required Mac permissions) for relay and pendant status queries.

Add a bridge liveness reconciler and stale-command janitor. Correlate extension heartbeat age, poll activity, pending-command count, command lease age, and the Mac agent's observed browser status instead of treating online=true as sufficient. Before dispatch, fail fast with a typed bridge_unavailable result when the last poll is stale; periodically expire/requeue orphaned commands whose 45-second lease elapsed, preserving idempotency keys so a late extension result cannot double-apply. Emit one deduplicated incident per outage and clear it on the first successful poll, with status exposed in /browser/status, /ops/status, /jobs, and the relay stream.

Add a health-aware browser command circuit breaker and queue reconciler. Before dispatch, consult the extension heartbeat/status; if offline or heartbeat stale, fail locally within ~1 second with a structured OFFLINE_BRIDGE result instead of waiting ~45 seconds. Mark queued commands as blocked (not failed), coalesce identical retries by idempotency key, and automatically resume only after a fresh heartbeat. Include bridge last-seen age, pending-command count, and a single reconnect instruction in the receipt and relay/pendant notification.

Add an offline-aware command lifecycle between the existing browser queue and job receipts. Before dispatching any browser_* action, read bridge liveness and, when offline, immediately persist a typed `waiting_for_browser` result (with health timestamp and no 45-second action timeout). Keep the original job/action id and park it rather than enqueueing duplicates. On POST /browser/heartbeat or the poll loop, claim parked actions atomically and resume incomplete IDs; write one receipt transition (`waiting_for_browser` → `running` → `completed|failed`). Emit a compact relay event for the transition so the pendant can speak the status, while `/jobs/:id` remains the source of truth.

Add lease/TTL semantics and supersession for browser commands: every queued command records session, prerequisite health snapshot, expiry, and supersedes key; when the extension is offline, coalesce repeated idempotent probes, stop dispatching stale work, and emit one deferred receipt. On heartbeat, revalidate the session before releasing only still-valid commands.

Add a browser-bridge liveness controller around the existing command queue: persist command lease/heartbeat timestamps, cap or back off retries, quarantine commands whose lease is stale or whose attempt count exceeds a threshold, and expose queue health (oldest age, claimed duration, attempts, last heartbeat, per-device online state) in /ops/status and the dashboard. When the bridge is offline or repeatedly times out, fail fast with a typed 'bridge_unhealthy' receipt instead of spending ~45 seconds per navigate and leaving nine commands pending; automatically requeue only after a fresh heartbeat, with idempotency preserved.

Add a bridge watchdog and failure-aware executor around browser actions. Before dispatch, issue a cheap local health snapshot (extension polling age, Safari frontmost/window state, tab/session id); attach it to the existing job and receipt. On timeout, stop waiting at a short staged deadline, classify offline vs no-answer vs page-load, and run a single read-only reattach/retry when the action is idempotent. Persist the original request id, retry lease, health snapshots, and final effect verdict so the dashboard and pendant can explain exactly what happened. Keep FULL_CONTROL_MODE and unrestricted capability unchanged; this is telemetry and recovery, not a blocking policy.

Add an offline-aware command lease and recovery controller for the Mac browser bridge. Every queued browser command gets createdAt, expiresAt, attempt count, idempotency key, and operation class. When /browser/status or /browser/heartbeat reports the extension offline, stop issuing duplicate retries; on reconnect, automatically replay only unexpired idempotent reads, coalesce identical pending reads, and move expired/failed navigations to a dead-letter record with the exact error and source job. Emit a single recovery receipt linking the original job, command, attempts, and final outcome, and expose pending/expired/dead-letter counts in /ops/status and /journal. This is observability and recovery, not an approval gate.

Add a stale-command quarantine ledger, separate from the pending browser queue: when an extension misses heartbeat, freeze delivery; assign each queued command an enqueue timestamp, originating utterance/job ID, tab/session affinity, and expiry; on reconnect, atomically classify each as safe-to-discard, safe-to-revalidate, or requires explicit replay. Revalidate tab URL/session and idempotency key before any replay, and expose a one-call pendant/dashboard summary plus discard-all-for-job operation. Do not execute or silently replay the current 12 pending commands.

Add an adaptive, evidence-preserving recovery layer specifically for browser navigation. Before browser_navigate, validate bridge heartbeat, session/tab affinity, and URL normalization; on failure classify the returned error as stale tab, extension transport timeout, blocked/unsupported URL, or page-load timeout. Retry only transient transport/page-load failures with the same idempotency key and bounded backoff, reattach the named session when possible, and use a safe Safari foreground/open-url fallback only for public URLs. Persist each attempt, error class, final URL/title, heartbeat age, and backend choice in the existing job receipt/journal. Never report navigation success from an enqueued command: success requires a post-navigation URL/title/readback, otherwise return a truthful partial failure with the next recovery action.

Develop an extension that securely coordinates real-time UI context between the Mac vision agent and the browser agent, enabling reliable browser automation even when API integration is insufficient or unavailable.

Give the relay a server-side browsing path using Cloudflare Browser Run for public web tasks, with a policy to prefer server_browser_actions over routing through the Mac when the target is public and doesn’t require the user’s authenticated sessions.

entries.summary: Implement a dual-path browser runner: authenticated Safari bridge when Mac is online, and Cloudflare Browser Run for public pages when it is not. Use a shared step model (navigate/read/extract/click) with provenance, typed results, and an idempotency key per request.

Implement the granted server_browser_actions schema using Cloudflare Browser Run as a fallback/alternative to the Mac browser extension. Provide a durable command queue, request ids, idempotency keys, typed results (page metadata, extracted text, screenshots), and explicit irreversible-action checkpoints. Allow public web reads when the Mac is offline; route authenticated/private pages only via the Mac Safari bridge.

Add a browser heartbeat and queue reconciler that reports explicit surface health (online/offline, accessibility trust, screen recording permission, command backlog). When unhealthy, stop claiming browser workflows and instead offer to queue work or switch to public web search.
Add a durable browser command queue with typed results and provenance (tabId, URL, timestamp, DOM locator) and support for server_browser_actions fallback when the Mac is offline.

Build a durable authenticated browser job runner that can execute typed actions (navigate, read, extract, fill) with tab/session affinity, idempotency keys, and typed results, plus a semantic diff layer for page-change detection.
Implement server_browser_actions using an isolated, ephemeral browser session with strict allowlists and artifact capture (DOM snapshot, extracted text, evidence links).

Add a SecretHandle channel between the authenticated browser extension and the Mac typing harness. The extension verifies origin, DOM field fingerprint, focus, and one-time expiry, then transfers only an opaque handle over an authenticated local channel. The Mac consumes the handle in a native secure-input primitive; planner, relay, screenshots, accessibility event logs, action receipts, and crash telemetry see only handle ID, field metadata, and outcome. Zeroize the handle after one successful or failed attempt and invalidate it on navigation or focus change.

Add a failure-aware resume coordinator above the browser and Mac queues. For every multi-step request, persist a checkpoint containing the last verified browser tab/page fingerprint, action idempotency key, evidence hash, and owner-visible side-effect state. Classify failures as offline, stale tab/session, transient navigation, authentication wall, semantic mismatch, or unknown; retry only transient cases with bounded backoff, never replay a side-effecting step without an unchanged precondition, and surface a pendant-sized 'paused—needs you' receipt. When connectivity returns, reconcile extension pending commands against relay/Mac receipts before resuming, eliminating duplicate execution such as repeated browser_navigate attempts.

Add an evidence-driven browser failure circuit breaker and resumable handoff. For each requestId/idempotencyKey, classify timeout, tab-disconnect, navigation-error, and auth-block separately; after two identical failures stop replaying the same command, capture current tab/session health and last evidence capsule, try exactly one safe alternate backend (authenticated Mac bridge versus server Browser Run when the page is public), then persist a checkpoint with the last confirmed URL/DOM hash and the next non-duplicating step. Emit a pendant-readable failure/recovery event and require confirmation before retrying any mutation.

Insert a Mac-local Context Firewall as the mandatory serialization boundary for browser inspection, research, capture enrichment, screenshots, clipboard text, and planner requests. It applies ordered detectors and an allowlist of semantic regions, replaces sensitive spans with typed redaction markers, emits a hash-only redaction manifest, and refuses any unclassified payload. Evidence capsules and pipeline events carry the manifest so downstream agents know exactly what they did not see.

Add an offline-command quarantine and recovery protocol on top of the browser queue: every queued command gets an expiry, retry budget, and dependency snapshot; when the extension is offline, the relay stops blind retries, marks commands stale, and sends one compact status event to the pendant. On reconnection, only idempotent reads are replayed automatically; mutations require a fresh approval and a before/after revalidation. Preserve the original request ID and produce a receipt explaining expired, replayed, or withheld work.

“What’s actually true right now?” Give me one compact, timestamped snapshot of what is on my Mac screen, which private browser tabs are open and readable, what the relay and wearable pipeline are doing, and whether any actions are still pending—separate observed facts from stale history and never claim a UI action succeeded unless its effect is verified.

“Test my pendant without LTE.” With the pendant and ESP32 bridge attached by USB, capture a short end-to-end loop: identify both serial devices, record button/audio/LED packets, send a signed synthetic command from the Mac bridge through the relay simulator, play a known PCM tone or sentence, and return a packet-level receipt showing what was observed locally versus what reached the cloud.

“Freeze this moment, and tell me what changed when I come back.” Capture a signed, read-only reality freeze of the Mac foreground app, browser tab identities and titles, relay/device connectivity, active pipeline/jobs, and permission reachability; later compare a fresh freeze and narrate only meaningful changes, including which changes are observations versus events recovered from history.

“Before you use the cloud, show me exactly what would leave my Mac.” For a task involving a logged-in page, microphone, screenshot, or local document, produce a field-level transfer manifest naming each datum, its source surface, destination/model, retention, and purpose; let me approve only selected fields or keep the whole task local.
“Before you tell me something happened, prove whether it is live, completed, merely rendered, or only historical—and say what evidence you used.”
“What can I safely rely on right now?”
“Watch for contradictions between what the Mac, browser, relay, and pendant claim, and interrupt me only when the contradiction could cause me to miss or repeat something.”
“Replay the last interaction exactly: what the pendant captured, what you heard, what each machine believed I asked, what was actually done, and where the handoff stopped.”
“For anything consequential, show me the proposed change on the Mac, then require a deliberate physical confirmation on my pendant before sending or submitting it.”
“When I lose connectivity, keep a private, ordered queue of what I asked and what still needs doing; when connection returns, ask me once about conflicts instead of silently replaying anything.”
“Tell me exactly why you refused, paused, or downgraded that request—and what single fact or permission would have let you continue.”
“What is actually available right now?” — give me one short, spoken status of my Mac, browser, relay, and pendant, separating live, stale, unavailable, and merely recorded history.
“Before you do anything on that website, verify that the tab is really the page I meant, loaded successfully, and still signed in; if not, tell me exactly what is wrong and stop.”

“Is this the right account before I do anything?” Have the system compare the identity, organization, and permissions visible across my open private tabs, then warn me if tabs are signed into different accounts or if the requested action would occur under the wrong identity.

“Run an end-to-end hearing check.” Send a known spoken test through the actual Mac-to-relay-to-pendant-to-ESP32 path, verify each hop and the 24 kHz/31.25 kHz/44.1 kHz format boundaries, then tell me exactly where it stopped—without storing the recording.

“Set up this pendant for me.” Put the physically connected nRF9160 and ESP32 into a named owner device, verify firmware identity and clock, enroll it with the relay, run a synthetic audio handshake, and refuse to call it ready until the owner-facing receipt proves which hops passed.

“Tune the pendant for my ears.” Play a short set of synthetic calibration tones through the actual ESP32/Bluetooth path, measure clipping, latency, dropouts, and perceived volume with my confirmation, then store a per-headphone playback profile that keeps speech intelligible without touching microphone recordings.

“What of mine is stored right now, and who can reach it?” Give me a live, plain-language inventory across pendant SD, Mac workspace, relay D1/R2, browser sessions, and generated audio: contents, retention, access surface, last access, and one-tap revoke/delete controls for each category.

When I ask you to act on my screen, first prove that the action channel is live; if Accessibility or Screen Recording is missing, explain exactly why and offer an AppleScript or browser-only alternative instead of pretending it worked.

If my pendant is disconnected, keep my request alive on the Mac and relay, then tell me when it was actually delivered to the wearable—not merely rendered or uploaded—and replay any missed response once the device reconnects.

Tell me whenever the system's records contradict one another—for example, a pipeline event says a pendant received audio while the live registry says no pendant exists—and show me the two source records instead of choosing one silently.

While I am in a meeting, let me ask “who is this, and what are we discussing?” and receive a private, confidence-labeled answer that fuses the pendant’s recent audio, my calendar invite, and the relevant authenticated browser or document tab—without saving the meeting by default.

When I return to my desk, ask “what changed while I was gone?” and get a timeline that combines only meaningful changes in my Mac apps, authenticated browser tabs, pending jobs, and pendant alerts, with one source citation for every item.

If I say “make sure that happened,” verify the complete chain from my spoken request to the final observable result: understand me on the pendant, inspect the right browser or Mac state, perform the approved step, and report evidence—or tell me exactly where the chain broke.

"What is actually happening right now?" Give me one short, spoken situational snapshot: what app is in front, what my browser has open, whether the relay/Mac bridge/pendant are reachable, and whether anything I asked for is running or waiting. Mark each fact fresh, stale, or unknown, and call out contradictions instead of guessing.

"Did that really work?" For my last request, independently verify the result across the machine, browser, relay, and audio delivery, then tell me exactly what is proven, what merely claimed success, and what still needs me.

"Why did that fail?" Build me a causal timeline for the request: speech received, plan made, actions attempted, approvals or permissions that blocked it, browser/relay handoffs, and final delivery. Separate the first failure from later symptoms and suggest the one next observation that would disambiguate it.

"Only do sensitive things when I am physically wearing the pendant." Use the pendant as a cryptographic presence-and-consent key: for sending messages, purchases, account changes, or exposing secrets, require a fresh hardware challenge and an intentional button hold, then show me exactly which action that proof authorizes.

"When I walk away from my Mac, protect me automatically, and restore my exact working context when I return." Detect pendant proximity loss and return using a secure local link; pause spoken output, hide or lock sensitive browser sessions, suspend queued actions, then restore only the tabs, job, and approval state that were active at departure.

"Tell me what I was doing when I left, without making me explain it again." At a physical transition—pendant disconnected, Mac closed, or pendant returned—create a private, evidence-backed checkpoint of the owner's active task: the relevant app and browser tab, unsent drafts, pending jobs, last spoken exchange, and unresolved approvals. On return, speak only the smallest useful resume prompt.
“I’m back—what was I doing, and what should I do next?” (or press the pendant button twice).

“Every morning, check my calendar, unread email, and today’s files, then give me a short spoken brief with the meetings that need preparation and a proposed priority list.”
entries.note: briefing.js: morning brief reads Calendar+Mail+recent files+Mac state, flags meetings needing prep, derives a priority list; spoken line + long-form audio + Notes.app note + markdown. Live-verified on the owner's real calendar/inbox.

entries.summary: “Clean up my Downloads every Friday: group files by project, rename obvious duplicates, and show me a review list before anything is deleted.”
entries.note: Duplicate of cap-0e0b8d35 + cap-52dcc328, both implemented in downloadsTidy.js: the Friday schedule, the dated grouping and the review-before-anything list are all there. Its two extra words are answered rather than skipped — duplicates are detected by content signature and REPORTED, never renamed or deleted, because 'obvious duplicate' is a guess and deletion is not reversible.

entries.summary: “Research this topic and leave me a concise source-linked briefing on my Mac, with an audio version I can play later.”

Audio is rendered at the pendant's exact wire format (24 kHz mono s16le + Ogg Opus) so it plays on the Mac or from the pendant later; ceiling is 120 s, not the 10 s reply cap. Verified: 71-85 s briefs produced.

entries.summary: “Every morning, give me a concise briefing of today’s calendar, unread priority messages, weather, and the files I need for my first meeting; let me ask follow-ups and open anything I mention.”

Two parts of the ask are NOT built: weather is not folded in (get_weather exists as a separate action), and 'the files I need for my first meeting' is a recency list, not per-meeting file matching. Follow-ups/'open anything I mention' are the normal conversational path, not this module.

entries.summary: “Prepare me for my next meeting: find the agenda and related local documents, summarize the open decisions and prior action items, and put the three most relevant files in a folder I can open.”
entries.note: meetingPrep.js. Retrieval, not summary: ranks local documents against the invite and quotes the sentences that already state a decision or an action, with their source file. Two bugs found and fixed against the owner's real data — a 5-minute solo alarm was being treated as 'the next meeting', and the organiser's own name matched every file on the machine. Verified live: found the real 9pm interview, 3 related documents copied into a folder with BRIEF.md. GET /meeting-prep. 14 tests.

entries.summary: “When I say ‘prepare my workday’, check my calendar and inbox, make a concise brief, and put it in a note on my Mac; don't send anything.”
entries.note: briefing.js kind=workday: 'prepare my workday' matches deterministically (no model call), reads Calendar+Mail, writes a Notes.app note and a markdown brief. Composes and stores only — assertNeverSends refuses any transmitting sink and there is no transport call in the module.

entries.summary: “Find the best flight options for next Thursday, compare total price and duration, and leave me a shortlist; do not book.”
entries.note: research.js (another agent, in this round) already is this capability: mode 'compare' gathers and verifies sources, and 'do not book' is structural there — no code path transacts, and assertNoTransactionClaim throws if the model even narrates a booking. Verified by running the actual flight query through POST /research: it returned a real nonstop-vs-connecting comparison for next Thursday with no booking. A second flight-specific ranker would duplicate it.

entries.summary: “Clean up my Downloads: group files by type into folders and show me what will be moved before doing it.”
entries.note: downloadsTidy.js. Preview and apply are two calls with the plan persisted between them, so apply replays exactly what the owner read rather than recomputing it; sources are re-stat'd and anything that changed is reported as drift and skipped. Nothing deletes, collisions are suffixed, every apply leaves an undo manifest. Verified against the owner's real ~/Downloads: 28 files previewed into 5 groups, NOTHING APPLIED. 16 tests.

entries.summary: “Every weekday at 5 pm, summarize the notes I created today into three next actions and put them in my task app; never send messages.”

entries.summary: “Give me a workday brief at 8:30, and let me play it from the pendant when I’m ready.”

entries.summary: “Research this topic, compare the best options, and leave me a short audio recommendation—don’t buy anything.”

'Don't buy anything' is built in, not a gate — no code path here can transact, the compose prompt forbids claiming otherwise, and assertNoTransactionClaim() rejects a brief that says it ordered/booked/paid (tested). The note states 'Nothing was bought, booked or ordered'. Verified live on portable power stations under $500.

entries.summary: “Every Friday, tidy my Downloads into dated folders, show me a preview, and only then apply it.”

Verified live: routine registered, force-run, planner emitted run_shell, preview written to the workspace, nothing moved.

entries.summary: Every weekday at 8:30, prepare a concise workday brief: today's calendar, unread mail grouped by urgency, and the top three actions; save it as an audio briefing I can play later.

entries.summary: When I say 'triage my inbox', classify unread mail into urgent, reply soon, reference, and noise, draft replies for the first two categories, and show me a reviewable list without sending anything.
entries.note: local-agent/mailTriage.js + POST /mail/triage, GET /mail/triage[/:id], triage_inbox action, and a deterministic matcher on 'triage my inbox' (no model needed to reach it). Unread mail is classified into urgent / reply soon / reference / noise, replies are drafted for the first two, and the whole thing is written to ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/mail-triage/<run>/REVIEW.md with one file per draft. NEVER SENDS, structurally: sinks go through briefing.js assertNeverSends, and assertScriptNeverSends refuses to hand osascript any script containing Mail's send verb. Drafts are markdown files, deliberately not Mail.app drafts, which are one keystroke from going out. Live against the owner's real 3,205-message inbox (109 unread over 60 days, 59s): the read is bounded by BOTH a date floor and a message cap and batches one Apple event per column, since the per-message form is what hung the connection before. Four classification bugs found and fixed against that real inbox: Hide My Email relays read as people, a bulk DOMAIN was being read as a marketing SENDER, and role addresses plus brand display names ('Valerie from Holafly', 'Premium*Tesla <Sales.SG@...>') earned drafted replies to adverts. Bodies for the drafted messages are read in a second pass by index with a subject re-check; verified live that a stale index is refused rather than drafted against.

entries.summary: Keep a daily 'closeout' routine: at 5:30 PM, summarize unfinished calendar items and the notes/files I touched today, then create a short checklist for tomorrow.
entries.note: Duplicate of cap-23af3e85. briefing.js kind=wrapup is precisely this closeout: sources are notes + calendar + files (the notes and files touched today, and the day's calendar), and its sinks are file + macnote + REMINDER — deriveNextActions writes real macOS Reminders, which is the 'short checklist for tomorrow'. routines.js schedules it at 17:30. It already excludes its own briefing notes so it stops assigning the owner homework about its own output.

Covered today: authenticated reads (as cap-c262d2f0) and POST /memory/browser-findings to persist normalized claims with provenance and TTL. GAP (2) CLOSED 2026-08-07 — local-agent/originFanOut.js readOrigins() (POST /origins/read): several authenticated origins read for one question, per-origin results with provenance, evidence age and partial success. MISSING: (1) NO REVIEW QUEUE — nothing in the repo has an item lifecycle (new / reviewed / dismissed); the three near-misses are not it: GET /watches/reports + ack is watch-scoped and diff-only, GET /forms/fills is a rolling list of 20 manifests with no state field, and memory facts have TTL and lastUsed but no review state. readOrigins returns a batch, it does not retain one; (3) no "needs attention" classifier over web content.

entries.summary: When I say 'clean up my desktop', group obvious screenshots and downloads into dated folders, but show me the proposed moves first.
entries.note: local-agent/folderSweep.js: surveyFolder / planSweep / formatSweep / applySweep / undoSweep, plus GET /sweep/survey, POST /sweep/preview, GET /sweep[/:planId], POST /sweep/:planId/apply, POST /sweep/:planId/undo, and the sweep_folder_preview / _apply / _undo action types. Real classification, not a name-based guess: half-finished downloads (.crdownload/.part/.tmp/~$ and zero-byte files at least a day old, so nothing mid-write is touched), byte-identical duplicates (size + 64 KB sample to find candidates, then a full sha256 to settle it, capped at 256 MB above which the match is reported as unconfirmed and never proposed for deletion), stale installers (with an /Applications lookup so it can say "cursor is already installed"), stale files, and screenshots. Dispositions: delete / archive / file / flag / keep. Duplicates are only proposed for deletion when the bytes are proven identical AND the name reads as a copy ("report (1).pdf" beside "report.pdf"); anything that merely shares content is reported and left alone. Destinations are resolved to a free name at preview time, so nothing is ever overwritten and the path the owner reads is the path the file lands at. THE PREVIEW ON THE OWNER REAL DESKTOP, live through the running agent: 588 loose files, 556 screenshots and screen recordings totalling ~10 GB proposed into Screenshots/YYYY-MM/, 27 stale files into Archive/YYYY-MM/, 5 left alone. Nothing was applied. That preview also found a real bug: this Mac names screenshots in Traditional Chinese, and 30-odd files called "截圖 ..." were being filed as merely stale - SCREENSHOT_NAME now covers zh/ja/ko/es/fr/de/ru/nl as well as English, which is the sort of thing only real files tell you. NOT a gate: applySweep never asks anything, there is no token or expiry on a plan (a test asserts that), and move_path/delete_path still run immediately through /execute exactly as before. Apply takes a planId because "do what you showed me" is only meaningful if the thing applied is the thing shown; it re-checks every source against the recorded size and mtime and reports drift rather than substituting a fresh guess, and it runs through the ordinary executor so each item leaves a receipt and an undo-vault snapshot. 18 node:test cases.

entries.summary: Clean up my Downloads: identify duplicate, temporary, and likely finished files, show me a proposed plan, then move only the approved items into an archive folder.
entries.note: Same module as cap-2eef696b: local-agent/folderSweep.js + the /sweep routes + sweep_folder_preview/_apply. This entry is the one that asked for all four parts by name, and all four are there. IDENTIFY: duplicate (size + 64 KB sample to shortlist, full sha256 to confirm, 256 MB cap above which it is reported unconfirmed and never deleted), temporary (.crdownload/.part/.partial/.download/.tmp/.aria2/~$ plus zero-byte files at least a day old), and likely finished (stale by mtime, default 90 days; stale installers at 30, with an /Applications lookup that says whether the app is already installed). SHOW ME A PROPOSED PLAN: POST /sweep/preview writes the plan and returns it with a formatted preview; nothing moves. MOVE ONLY THE APPROVED ITEMS: POST /sweep/:planId/apply takes an "only" list of item ids, so the owner who read twelve lines and wants three gets three - a selection, not a permission; naming an id that is not in the plan is an error rather than a fresh decision. INTO AN ARCHIVE FOLDER: Archive/YYYY-MM/ (Installers/ subfolder for those), Screenshots/YYYY-MM/ for captures. LIVE ON THE OWNER REAL ~/Downloads, preview only, nothing applied: 28 loose files, no duplicates, 3 screenshots from July proposed into Screenshots/2026-07/, 24 active files correctly left alone at the 90-day default. At a 21-day threshold it also picks up Cursor-darwin-universal.dmg (410 MB) with the reason "cursor is already in /Applications; installer last touched 10 days ago". The restraint is the point: an agent that moved all 28 would have been wrong. Not a gate - applySweep asks nothing, holds no token, and every direct file action still executes immediately.

'Never send anything without showing me the drafts first' is the product shape, not a gate — the drafts are files under ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/mail-triage/<run>/drafts/ carrying To/Subject/In-Reply-To and the line 'Status: DRAFT - not sent, not queued, not in Mail.app'. Verified live: a real unread message, its real body read out of Mail, a real model-written draft signed with the name the owner's Mail account sends under, on disk, nothing transmitted.

entries.note: local-agent/meetingFollowup.js + POST /meeting-followup, meeting_followup action, deterministic matcher on 'after my meeting' / 'meeting follow-up'. Finds the meeting that most recently ENDED (one still running is left alone), opens the meeting notes and a SUMMARY-DRAFT.md next to them, and lists the unread mail matching that meeting. The extraction is meetingPrep.js's, imported not copied, so both halves of a meeting agree about what an action item is. Never sends — assertNeverSends on the sinks, and the summary says so in its own first line. Live on the owner's real calendar: found 'Summer Interview with Evan between Evan Liu and Aditya Pall', wrote the workspace, read real notes. Two bugs found against that real data: it first opened meetingPrep's own COPY of a transcript (copying resets mtime, so agent output looked like notes typed during the meeting — same lesson as briefing.js's isBriefingNote), and the notes window opened at the nominal calendar start, missing a Zoom chat saved at 21:46 for a 22:00 meeting.

entries.summary: “Once a week, clean up my Downloads: group files by type and project, flag duplicates and stale installers, and show me a review list before anything is deleted.”
entries.note: Covered by local-agent/folderSweep.js (see cap-2b03a27d), with the two parts this entry adds that nothing else had. FLAG DUPLICATES AND STALE INSTALLERS: downloadsTidy.js already reported duplicates, but had no notion of an installer going stale; classifyFile now tags installer / stale-installer / already-installed by checking /Applications, which on the owner real Downloads produced "cursor is already in /Applications; installer last touched 10 days ago" for a 410 MB dmg. A REVIEW LIST BEFORE ANYTHING IS DELETED: the delete section of the preview is separated from the move sections and each line carries its reason, and deletes go through the executor so each one is snapshotted into the undo vault first and undoSweep puts the bytes back - verified by a test that deletes a .crdownload and restores it. GROUP BY TYPE: yes, via the disposition classes and downloadsTidy planTidy groupBy=type/date. GROUP BY PROJECT: NOT BUILT - inferring which project a loose download belongs to needs projectMemory/contextGraph and is a different piece of work; nothing here guesses at it. ONCE A WEEK: the scheduler already exists (routines.js + POST /routines), and sweep_folder_preview is a plannable action type, so a weekly routine can be created without new code; no routine was created, since standing configuration on the owner machine is theirs to set up. Overlaps cap-0e0b8d35 / cap-b4dfb9ea / cap-52dcc328, which another subagent took for the group-by-type/date half in downloadsTidy.js; this entry is filed implemented rather than duplicate because the duplicate-confidence, stale-installer and review-before-delete parts are only in folderSweep.js.

entries.note: briefing.js kind=mail, reachable as 'Summarize what I missed in my email today.' Deterministic route, 24h-bounded Mail query, separates priority mail from newsletters. Live output: 'Good morning. 3 unread emails, all newsletters.'

entries.summary: “Read my upcoming schedule for the day.”
entries.note: briefing.js kind=schedule, reachable as 'Read my upcoming schedule for the day.' Deterministic route, renders long-form audio. Live output: 'Good morning. 7 meetings today, next is stand up at 9:00 AM. 2 need preparation.'

entries.summary: “Save this idea for later.”
entries.note: quickCapture.js: 'save this idea for later' parses off the lead-in and stores the idea whole. Two stores by design — memoryService (prompt tier, sensitivity-aware) and contextGraph (durable archive) — so an idea neither expires nor leaks. POST /capture, GET /capture?query=, action type quick_capture. 12 tests.

entries.summary: “Plan my day. Pull my calendar, summarize critical tasks and travel time, and give me a 30-second briefing.”
entries.note: dayPlan.js. Calendar+Reminders read through EventKit (appleData.js) because Calendar.app's AppleScript walks all 16 calendars per query. Briefing is built against a spoken word budget and drops whole sentences, never mid-sentence. Travel is the real gap between real places — a Zoom URL is not somewhere you travel to. Verified live: 3 events, 25 tasks, 48 words / ~17s inside a 30s target. GET /day-plan. 9 tests.

entries.summary: “Read my notifications and tell me only what’s important.”
entries.note: notificationTriage.js. Notification Center's DB needs Full Disk Access and logs dismissed banners anyway, so it triages the three sources that generate the interruptions: unread mail, imminent meetings, overdue reminders. Default is silence — everything must earn a threshold. Verified live: scanned 83, surfaced 2 past-due, suppressed 80, in 4.3s. 10 tests.

entries.summary: “Start a focus session for 25 minutes. Block distractions and let me know when time’s up.”
entries.note: focusSession.js. End time written to disk before anything is blocked, so the alarm survives a restart (resumeFocusSessions re-arms, or fires late rather than dropping). Blocking hides apps reversibly and restores only what this session changed. Verified live: hid Mail+Spotify in 0.6s, auto-ended at 2 min, spoke the alarm, restored both. 9 tests.

entries.summary: “Remember this: my bike lock code is 4829.”
entries.note: Same module. 'my X is Y' becomes a keyed fact; a spoken lock code is classified secret by new patterns in redaction.js, so the value lives in exactly one 0600 file and contextProjection renders it 'bike lock code: [withheld]' in prompts while the owner reads 4829 back in full. Verified live: 0 occurrences in context_graph.json, 1 in facts.json.

entries.summary: “Summarize the key points from this page and read them to me later.”
entries.note: mode=page: readOpenTabs() drives browser_list_tabs + browser_read_page over POST /execute, so pages are read in the owner's real logged-in profile, then summarized into key points and rendered to audio they play later. Falls back to the public web when no tab matches rather than failing. Verified live against open Safari tabs (2 tabs read, 78.6 s of audio).

entries.summary: "Summarize this webpage" or "Check the price on this product"
entries.note: Same capability and same code path as cap-d9af189b (mode=page): read the page the owner already has open and summarize it. Immediate delivery is the --now flag on the same command; price-on-this-product is that summary of the open product page. No separate implementation.

entries.summary: "Remind me to do X at 6 pm" or "Every weekday at 9, remind me to stand up"
entries.note: remindMe.js. One-off -> Apple Reminders (reused reminders.js, not a second path). Recurring -> a repeating Calendar event with an alarm, because routines.js cannot express 'not on Saturday' and only fires while the agent is up. Verified live: real Reminders item due Fri 18:00, real event 'stand up' FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR at 09:00 with 1 alarm. 9 tests.

entries.summary: “Check the weather and read the highlights to me.”
entries.note: Already built, outside the briefing family: policyRouter.js has a get_weather deterministic matcher (no model call), computerControl dispatches it to local-agent/builtins/weather.js, which fetches wttr.in and returns a one-line current-conditions summary that pendantSpeech.js reads aloud. That is the whole ask as stated. Worth naming the ceiling rather than reopening it: wttr.in format=3 is one line of CURRENT conditions, so 'the highlights' is today's weather, not a multi-day forecast or a set of ranked alerts. Also noted on cap-c071fa0a: weather is a standalone action and is NOT folded into briefing.js's morning brief.

entries.summary: “When I get back to my desk, summarize what happened while I was away and queue anything urgent.”
entries.note: "When I get back to my desk, summarize what happened while I was away" is now the deferral path in cloud-relay/routines.js. A routine that needs the Mac (calendar, mail, notes, files, screen) and comes due while the lid is closed is NOT failed and NOT faked by the relay: chooseVenue returns 'defer', the occurrence is held with its original dueAt and retried each minute, and it runs the moment the bridge heartbeat returns — then its answer becomes a spoken announcement. Bounded at 12 h so a long absence drops the occurrence with a 'missed' receipt instead of firing a pile of stale briefings at once. Verified live: Mac-venue routine dispatched, the bridge ran it, reapDispatchedRuns turned the result into a pending announcement.

entries.summary: “Remind me every weekday at 5 to shut down and summarize what I did today.”
entries.note: "Remind me every weekday at 5" is expressible and durable: {kind:'weekly', at:'17:00', days:['weekdays']} in cloud-relay/routineSchedule.js, with an IANA timezone because a Worker runs in UTC and a naive setHours(17) would fire at 11am Central. DST-stable (two-pass offset resolution, tested across the 2026-11-01 transition). The summarize half runs on the Mac when it is awake and defers when it is not (cap-64c3562b). Reaching the pendant unprompted at 5pm still needs firmware — see the README section 'How an announcement reaches the pendant'; today the brief is spoken the moment the next press opens the socket.

entries.summary: “Read me the top three things I should care about right now.”
entries.note: Duplicate of cap-f66f7f6e (local-agent/notificationTriage.js, GET /notifications, triage_notifications action). It scores the three sources that actually generate interruptions — unread mail, an imminent meeting, an overdue reminder — against one threshold, sorts by score and speaks the top items, saying how many it skipped. That is 'the top three things I should care about right now'; the ranking and the spoken form already exist and the default is silence when nothing clears the bar. Verified live in this round: it returned two past-due reminders and suppressed 80 other items.

entries.summary: Give me a quick briefing for my day, and make it something I can listen to later.
entries.note: Duplicate of cap-1634d96f (dayPlan.js, GET /day-plan — the day built against a spoken word budget) and cap-2a60c5ba (audioBrief.js, which renders every briefing to .wav/.opus at the pendant's 24 kHz mono wire format and keeps it on the shelf under ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/Briefings until it is played). 'Quick briefing for my day' and 'something I can listen to later' are those two, already joined: POST /briefing composes and audioBrief stores.

entries.summary: Look up this topic on the web and summarize it for me.
entries.note: Duplicate of cap-9764ec65 (local-agent/research.js). It searches the public web, FETCHES AND READS each candidate page — a URL nothing opened is never cited — and composes a cited brief on the cheap text tier. POST /research, the research-brief.mjs CLI and routines all reach it. 'Look up this topic and summarize it' is the plain-brief mode of exactly that.

entries.summary: “Summarize the top results from the web about X, and keep it out of my Mac.”

entries.summary: “Keep an eye on this website and let me know when anything important changes.”

entries.summary: “Give me a quick overnight briefing.”
entries.note: Covered by: worker-scheduler

entries.summary: “Every morning, give me a 30-second audio digest of what changed: calendar, reminders, and top emails.”
"Queue this up and tell me when it’s done" (for example: summarize a long document, compare options, draft an email, or research a topic).
“When I press the pendant button, capture a short voice note, tag it with time and place if available, and later summarize it into tasks.”
“I asked you to handle that on my Mac—what’s the status?”
entries.note: Shipped as the relay_job_status Realtime tool (7th tool in REALTIME_TOOLS), backed by the new cloud-relay/jobRecall.js. Note was empty before this; nothing to preserve. Voice path end to end: openaiRealtimeVoice.js answers the tool INSIDE the turn like web_search — it never sets state.actions, so a status question dispatches no Mac job — and both session call sites inject the lookup (cloud-relay/server.js /v1/pendant/command, cloud-relay/pendantConverse.js duplex WS). SOURCE: relay job records via store.listJobs({type:'plan'}), not the Mac journal. Deliberate: the relay already holds the Mac's returned result/error for every job it dispatched, it is in-process (no round trip inside a spoken turn), and it still answers when the Mac is asleep — which is exactly the case where 'your Mac never picked it up' is the true answer. local-agent /journal is richer per action but needs a live bridge round trip and is not in OPS_ALLOWED_PREFIXES. REFERENCE HEURISTIC: explicit jobId wins; only type='plan' jobs are candidates (agent_proxy is plumbing, audio_capture is a spoken reply with no Mac work); deictics and status-question scaffolding are stripped to nothing before scoring so 'that'/'the thing I asked earlier' contribute zero evidence; content overlap x10 dominates recency; recency+unfinished only break ties; a reference that DID name something but matched nothing resolves to nothing rather than falling back to the newest job; with no content words, candidates older than 30 min are dropped; near-ties are flagged ambiguous and the spoken line always NAMES the task so a wrong pick is correctable in the next breath. HONESTY: describeJobOutcome is the single place that decides success. Terminal status with no result => 'unknown', and executed:false => 'failed' — the voiceRunForCapture bug (hardcoded success, silent runs reported completed) is covered by two regression tests. Approval gates report as awaiting_approval; queued past 60s reports as 'your Mac hasn't picked it up'. No approval gates or confirmation prompts added. SPOKEN: one sentence, hard-capped at 180 chars (same clip bridge.js uses), relative times ('3 minutes ago'), never JSON. TESTS: 21 in cloud-relay/jobRecall.test.js + 1 schema test in openaiRealtimeVoice.test.js. Two drift guards updated six->seven: openaiRealtimeVoice.test.js and local-agent/stackAlignment.test.js. Full suite green (832/832). NOT VERIFIED: no live OpenAI Realtime turn was run (needs an API key and the pendant), and the live Mac agent's job store is token-gated so real owner jobs were not read; the real query was run against the real cloud-relay in-memory store through the exact lookupJobStatus closure. Worker not deployed.
